corrections.original_claim: root_causes_observed[1]: "Click and the trustworthiness Python fixture both declare tests as methods (OracleTests::test_*, and Click's pytest-style module-level functions are the exception that does qualify structurally, but still fails on the cross-file rule above)."
corrections.problem: Self-contradictory as written: it opens by grouping Click with 'tests as methods', then immediately says Click's tests are module-level functions, not methods.
corrections.corrected_statement: The trustworthiness Python fixture declares its tests as methods of a class (OracleTests::test_*), which the extractor's top-level-only rule excludes regardless of file. Click's declared tests (tests/test_commands.py, tests/test_chain.py) are ordinary module-level pytest functions, not methods — they qualify under the top-level-only rule but still cannot reach Must because they are in a different file from Group.invoke (src/click/core.py), the cross-file limitation already stated as its own root cause. The two fixtures fail for two different, independently-sufficient reasons; Click's failure is not an example of the top-level/method restriction at all.
